claims: C1: In the worked example, when the user steps off-screen while cooking and no danger is yet visible, saying nothing is good and issuing a premature warning is bad.
C2: In the worked example, when smoke becomes visible, issuing a warning is good and saying nothing is bad.
C3: The example illustrates the unclear-cases wait rule: in unclear cases the assistant should wait until there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent before interjecting.

concepts.name: video_interjection_rule
concepts.gloss: R is the rule that the assistant should interject when it identifies something on camera that could cause imminent bodily harm or death to the user.

concepts.name: unclear_cases_wait_rule
concepts.gloss: R is the rule that in unclear cases the assistant should wait until there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent before interjecting.

concepts.name: user_off_screen_cooking
concepts.gloss: S is a situation in the video where the user has stepped off-screen while food is cooking on a lit stove.

concepts.name: visible_smoke
concepts.gloss: S is a situation in the video where dark black smoke is visible coming from the pan.

concepts.name: premature_warning
concepts.gloss: W is a warning issued before there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent, such as warning about an unattended pan while the user is still off-screen and no smoke is visible.

concepts.name: timely_warning
concepts.gloss: W is a warning issued when there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent, such as warning about smoke coming from the pan.

concepts.name: good_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response marked as GOOD in the example comparison.

concepts.name: bad_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response marked as BAD in the example comparison.

concepts.name: situation_has
concepts.gloss: Situation S has property P, where P is one of the situation classes such as user_off_screen_cooking or visible_smoke.
concepts.inference: The example describes two distinct situations; a relation between a situation and its properties is needed to express the conditions.

concepts.name: response_in_situation
concepts.gloss: Response R is given in situation S.
concepts.inference: The example pairs each response with a situation; a relation linking a response to its situation is needed.

ontology.gloss: R is a response marked GOOD in the example.
R is a response marked BAD in the example.
ontology.body: response_in_situation(R, S), situation_has(S, user_off_screen_cooking), issue_warning(R), premature_warning(R)

asserts.read_back: In the example, saying nothing when the user steps off-screen while cooking is good because the case is unclear and no danger is yet visible.
In the example, issuing a premature warning when the user steps off-screen while cooking is bad because the case is unclear and the warning is premature.
In the example, issuing a timely warning when smoke becomes visible is good because there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent.
In the example, saying nothing when smoke becomes visible is bad because there is sufficient signal that danger is imminent and the assistant should interject.

closure.reason: The example marks saying nothing as good in the unclear off-screen case and bad when smoke is visible, but does not state a general rule for saying nothing outside these example situations.
The example marks a premature warning as bad and a timely warning as good, but does not state a general rule for issuing warnings outside these example situations.
